summary: Stefan M. Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen (1987) and habilitated at Freie Universität Berlin (1993). He became Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University in 1995.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor of religion in Asia and director of the Centre for the Study of Religion and Culture in Asia at the University of Groningen (~2013-2020) and joined SOAS around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning degrees at Ca' Foscari University of Venice under Maurizio Scarpari, Giuliano Boccali, and Alfredo Cadonna. He held positions at Soka University, Ca' Foscari, and served as Yehan Numata Professor at Oxford (2012-2020).

Steffen Döll is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich, where he was later an assistant (2008-2015), and became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch studied art history at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. A specialist in Indology and history/archaeology, she taught at Visva-Bharati University, Calcutta University, the University of Pennsylvania (1950-1993), and curated at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Sten Konow was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sophus Bugge at Oslo and Richard Pischel at Halle. He held posts as Government Epigraphist for India, professor at the University of Hamburg (1914-1919), and professor at the University of Oslo (1910-1937).
Stephan Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned degrees from Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, and studied under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy. She served as faculty at the University of Vermont (1991-2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who earned her doctorate at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She taught at Harvard University and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in 2002.

Stephen A. Murphy works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London, where he also pursued doctoral studies under Elizabeth H. Moore.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Harvard and the University of Michigan, he held professorships in art history and humanities at the University of Kansas (1977-1992) and the University of Richmond (1992-2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies and philosophy author. He studied with teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim at Songgwangsa, led Sharpham College (~1992-2000), and joined the core faculty of Bodhi College in 2015.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who held a Fulbright Junior Fellowship at the University of Kelaniya. His appointments include a visiting fellowship at Ruhr University Bochum and an associate professorship at Missouri State University (attested 2013).
Stephen Cook is a computer scientist who studied under Hao Wang (~1961-1966).

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University under Alan Sponberg, Denis Twitchett, and Daniel L. Overmyer. After Middlebury College, he became D. T. Suzuki Professor at Princeton in 1988.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt. He founded the Anthropos Institute and the Institute of Indian Culture, and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950-1954).

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone at Princeton University (~1995-2001) and joined the faculty at Western Michigan University around 2003.

Stephen G. Williams is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Colorado State University under Andre Archie, studied at the University of Oxford, and held a post at Worcester College, Oxford.
